title: A Son of Kerala Is About to Make World Cup History — in Qatar's Colours
excerpt: Tahsin Mohammed Jamshid, the Doha-born winger with roots in Kannur, stands on the brink of becoming the first footballer of Indian origin to play at a FIFA World Cup.
body:
For generations, the FIFA World Cup has been a festival in Kerala. Every four years, villages across Malabar transform into miniature football capitals — giant cut-outs of Brazilian and Argentine stars tower over paddy fields, midnight screenings draw thousands, and the debates over Pelé, Maradona and Messi never quite end. Yet through all that devotion, the state that loves the game most fiercely has never had one of its own on the sport's grandest stage.

That is about to change. As Qatar prepare to face co-hosts Canada at BC Place in Vancouver, a 20-year-old winger named Tahsin Mohammed Jamshid stands on the verge of history. If he steps onto the pitch at this 2026 World Cup, staged across the United States, Canada and Mexico, he will become the first player of Malayali origin — and the first footballer of Indian origin — ever to appear in a World Cup match.

**From Thalassery to Doha**

Tahsin was born in Qatar on June 16, 2006, to Malayali parents from Kannur district. His father, Jamshid, hails from Thalassery; his mother, Shyma, from Valapattanam. The family had moved to Qatar in 1996, part of the vast Malayali expatriate community that has helped build the Gulf over the past half-century. Football, though, was always in the blood. Jamshid was a talented player himself, representing the University of Calicut before emigrating, and it was under his father's guidance that Tahsin first picked up the game on Doha's training grounds.

His rise has been steady and, in retrospect, remarkable. He came through the prestigious Aspire Academy, the same system that has produced much of Qatar's senior squad, and broke into the country's Under-16 setup in 2021. He progressed through the Under-17 and Under-19 ranks before signing for Qatar Stars League heavyweights Al-Duhail, one of the most successful clubs in the Gulf. In doing so, he became the first footballer of Indian origin to play in the Qatari top flight.

In March 2024, Tahsin made his senior debut for Al-Duhail against Al Rayyan. Three months later he earned his first senior international cap for Qatar, coming on in a World Cup qualifier against Afghanistan. A quick, creative left winger with an eye for goal, he had already caught the attention of national selectors at the AFC Under-20 Asian Cup in China, where he featured in all three of Qatar's matches.

**A bittersweet kind of history**

There is a poignancy to the milestone that is not lost on Kerala's football fraternity. Tahsin will make history for India not in India's colours, but in Qatar's. He holds Qatari citizenship and has committed his international future to the country where he was born and raised. India, meanwhile, remains as far from a World Cup as ever — its men's team has never qualified, and its long-cherished dream of reaching football's biggest tournament feels no closer.

Yet for a state that has lived and breathed the game for decades, the symbolism is powerful regardless of the flag. Notably, Tahsin was once named in a Qatar squad for a match against India, though he did not take the field that day — a near-miss that only sharpens the sense of crossed destinies. Now, on the World Cup stage itself, a young man whose family tree runs through the sevens football grounds of Malabar carries a piece of Kerala with him.

**The moment that could come in Vancouver**

Qatar arrive in Vancouver in better shape than many predicted. After exiting the 2022 World Cup they hosted without a single point, they opened this campaign with a dramatic stoppage-time 1-1 draw against Switzerland in California, earning their first-ever World Cup point. Canada, the co-hosts, were held to an identical 1-1 scoreline by Bosnia and Herzegovina. With all four teams in Group B level on a point, a win for Qatar would move them to the brink of the knockout rounds under the expanded 48-team format.

Julen Lopetegui's side are likely to lean on familiar names — the gifted Akram Afif and the prolific Almoez Ali chief among them — and a disciplined, counter-attacking approach designed to frustrate Canada's pace. Whether Tahsin features will be the manager's call. But for thousands of Malayalis settled across North America and the Gulf, and for the football-mad towns back home in Kannur, the prospect alone is enough. After a lifetime of cheering for other people's countries, Kerala finally has a son to watch for. His name is Tahsin Jamshid, and the world is about to learn it.

nri_angle: For decades, football-obsessed Kerala has poured its passion into supporting Brazil, Argentina and Germany at the World Cup without ever having a player of its own on the stage. Tahsin Jamshid — born in Doha to Malayali parents from Kannur — is poised to become the first footballer of Indian origin to play at a FIFA World Cup, a landmark for the Gulf's vast Malayali expatriate community and a bittersweet milestone for an India whose own men's team has never qualified.
author: Diaspora Desk
